title: WHO Director-General Tedros Visits DRC — Confirmed Cases Nearly Double as Outbreak Accelerates
detail: WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus arrived in Bunia, Ituri Province on 30 May 2026, making his first in-country visit to the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus outbreak. The visit coincided with a dramatic surge in lab-confirmed case counts: DRC's Ministry of Health reported approximately 225 lab-confirmed cases as of May 30 — nearly double the 125 confirmed on May 29, representing the fastest 48-hour confirmation rate since the outbreak began. The jump reflects a combination of accelerated laboratory throughput (three additional mobile BSL-3 units became operational in Ituri between May 28–30) and genuine epidemic spread, not only a reclassification effect. Uganda's Ministry of Health simultaneously updated its confirmed case count to 9 lab-confirmed (up from 7 on May 29), with all cases linked to DRC travel or DRC-connected contacts in Kampala. Total suspected cases in DRC stood at approximately 1,028 as of May 30, with suspected deaths exceeding 220. Dr. Tedros met with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi and Health Minister Dr. Samuel Kasongo Mwamba, calling for 'maximum mobilization' of international resources. In his statement from Bunia, Tedros said: 'I came here to see with my own eyes, and to make clear to the international community that what is happening here demands an urgent and coordinated global response.' He visited the Bunia ETU and held a briefing with MSF field teams. The DG also addressed the WHO ring vaccination challenge directly, acknowledging the expert panel ruling and committing to fast-track the clinical trial framework for ChAdOx1 BDBV and therapeutic candidates within 21 days.

title: DRC Confirmed Cases Surge to ~225 — Fastest Lab-Confirmation Rate Since Outbreak Began
detail: By 30 May 2026, DRC Ministry of Health figures compiled in real-time by Al Jazeera, ECDC, and WHO's situation tracking page showed approximately 225 lab-confirmed cases in DRC — a near-doubling from 125 confirmed on May 29. The acceleration reflects both expanded laboratory capacity (three CDC-supported mobile BSL-3 labs now operational across Ituri, bringing total daily testing capacity to ~240 samples/day) and genuine outbreak acceleration driven by the uncaptured Mongbwalu patient cluster. WHO Situation Report tracking indicated approximately 1,028 suspected DRC cases as of May 30, with suspected deaths exceeding 220 in DRC alone. Uganda's confirmed count rose to 9 — two new confirmed cases identified in Kampala contacts of previously known DRC-linked cases, both rapidly isolated. CDC confirmed U.S. airport Ebola screening at Dulles, Atlanta, IAH, and JFK remains in effect, having processed over 11,000 passengers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan screening routes since the May 18 activation of the rerouting protocol. Contact tracing coverage in DRC remained below 50%, with the Mongbwalu cluster's 25+ escaped patients still representing an uncaptured transmission nucleus. The WHO expert panel framework for ChAdOx1 BDBV clinical trials — following the May 28 Ervebo ring vaccination halt — was reported to be finalized within 3 weeks, with trial sites proposed at Bunia and Kampala.
